properties.name: weakcrypto:config
properties.value: skill pq-crypto, 2 scouts, max iterations 400, build bbcd802706e4

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: BIP38 paper-wallet private-key import (decryptNoEC and decryptEC-multiply modes). AES-256-ECB/NoPadding is mandated by the BIP38 cross-wallet specification — each 16-byte block is XOR-masked with scrypt output by design, which mitigates ECB pattern leakage. Changeable only via a BIP38 protocol revision, not by this project alone. Grover halves the 256-bit key to a 128-bit quantum margin.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Implements Bitcoin Script's OP_SHA1 opcode — a consensus rule every validating node must honour, so the digest cannot be removed or swapped without a chain fork. No security decision of this library relies on it; observable/protocol-bound rather than changeable here. Migration is a Bitcoin-ecosystem decision (retiring the opcode), not a project-local fix.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The Bitcoin signature curve: every key, address, HD wallet path and transaction signature in this library is ECDSA over secp256k1, fixed by Bitcoin consensus. Migration to ML-DSA/SLH-DSA is an ecosystem-wide protocol transition on the Bitcoin roadmap, not a project-local change — changeable here only insofar as this library follows it.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: GraalVM native-image reflection registration for the wallettool native build: makes DSA key interfaces and DSAParameterSpec instantiable in the shipped binary (JCA keystore/serialization machinery can request them). Availability declaration, not an operation — the image ships the capability whether or not the application exercises it. Changeable by trimming the registration, but the JDK's KeyStore code is why they are listed.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: GraalVM native-image reflection registration for the wallettool native build: makes RSA key interfaces available in the shipped binary for standard JCA keystore handling. No active RSA encrypt/sign path exists in this tree; the asset is the capability the binary ships. Same availability class as the adjacent DSA registration.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: HMAC-SHA-512 is the PRF of the entire BIP32/BIP39 wallet stack: master key derivation from the seed ("Bitcoin seed" tag), child key derivation keyed by the chain code, and the round function of the homegrown PBKDF2SHA512 for BIP39 seeds. Fixed by the BIP32/BIP39 specifications; 512-bit digest leaves a 256-bit MAC under Grover — no migration pressure, a healthy asset.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: BIP39 mnemonic-to-seed derivation: PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA512, 2048 iterations, 64-byte output, salt "mnemonic"+passphrase. 2048 rounds is fixed by the BIP39 specification (all wallets' test vectors depend on it) and is defensible because the input is 128-256 bits of entropy, not a human password; the below-guidance iteration count is already carried by the PBKDF2-low-iterations object. The KDF itself is a homegrown clean-room PBKDF2SHA512 (RFC 2898 reference), which is why it lives in first-party code

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Every key byte in this library is generated from java.security.SecureRandom or from the kernel CSPRNG via the bundled LinuxSecureRandom SecureRandomSpi, which reads /dev/urandom and installs itself as JVM provider #1 on Linux (a global override — a posture control, and good practice). Uses: EC key generation, wallet seed entropy, scrypt salts, and per-encryption AES IVs. The "?" rating resolves to practice-conformant CSPRNG with no weak-RNG concern.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Bundled JKS CA trust store (cacerts) shipped inside the bitcoinj-core artifact as a classpath resource — historically the SSL/TLS trust anchors for platforms without a JVM default trust store (Android). In this tree it is unreferenced dead weight that still ships root CA certificates in the jar: a stale PKI/governance artifact worth wiring up or dropping from the build.
